messages.content: I want an API that takes an IP address and returns company data with contact information if available.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve data. This function is commonly used for API calls and web scraping. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The Date Nager API provides access holiday information for over 100 countries, including the ability to query for long weekends. It leverages ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to tailor the search to your specific region of interest. More information can be found in https://date.nager.at/Api

headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide to a handful of public IP‑lookup APIs that return **company‑level data** (name, domain, industry, size, logo, social links, etc.) and, where available, contact‑style fields such as email, phone, or website. All of the examples below use the `requests` library in Python, but you can translate them to `curl`, JavaScript, Go, etc. as needed. | # | Service | Endpoint (example) | Free tier | Key required? | Company / Contact fields returned | Notes | |---|---------|--------------------|-----------|---------------|----------------------------------|-------| | 1 | **ipdata.co** | `https://api.ipdata.co/?api-key=` | 1 000 req/day (free) | Yes (but you can use the demo key `demo` for testing) | `company`: `{name, domain, industry, size, description, logo_url, website, twitter, linkedin, facebook, instagram, youtube, github, blog}`
Top‑level: `org`, `asn`, `city`, `region`, `country_name`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `postal`, `timezone` | Richest company data; demo key works for up to 1 000 requests/day. | | 2 | **ipgeolocation.io** | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=&ip=` | 1 000 req/day (free) | Yes (demo key `YOUR_DEMO_KEY` works for 1 000 req/day) | `organization`: `{name, domain, industry, size, description, logo_url, website, twitter, linkedin, facebook, instagram, youtube, github, blog}`
Top‑level: `ip`, `continent_name`, `country_name`, `state_prov`, `city`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `zipcode`, `time_zone`, `asn`, `isp` | Similar to ipdata.co; demo key available. | | 3 | **ipstack.com** | `http://api.ipstack.com/?access_key=` | 10 000 req/month (free) | Yes (demo key `YOUR_DEMO_KEY` works for 10 000 req/month) | `company`: `{name, domain, industry, size, description, logo_url, website, twitter, linkedin, facebook, instagram, youtube, github, blog}`
Top‑level: `ip`, `continent_code`, `continent_name`, `country_code`, `country_name`, `region_code`, `region_name`, `city`, `zip`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `time_zone`, `currency`, `languages`, `as`, `asn`, `isp` | Good balance of free quota and depth. | | 4 | **ipapi.co** | `https://ipapi.co//json/?key=` | 30 000 req/month (free) | Yes (demo key `YOUR_DEMO_KEY` works for 30 000 req/month) | `org`, `asn`, `city`, `region`, `country_name`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `postal`, `timezone`, `readme` | Does *not* expose a dedicated “company” object, but `org` often contains the company name. | | 5 | **ipinfo.io** | `https://ipinfo.io//json?token=` | 50 000 req/month (free) | Yes (demo token `YOUR_DEMO_TOKEN` works for 50 000 req/month) | `org`, `hostname`, `city`, `region`, `country`, `loc`, `postal`, `timezone`, `readme` | `org` contains the company name + ASN; no separate contact fields. | --- ## Quick‑start example (Python) ```python import requests def get_company_info(ip, api_key="demo"): """ Query ipdata.co for company data. Replace `demo` with your own API key for production use. """ url = f"https://api.ipdata.co/{ip}" params = {"api-key": api_key} resp = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5) resp.raise_for_status() # raise an exception for non‑200 status codes data = resp.json() # Extract useful fields company = data.get("company", {}) result = { "ip": data.get("ip"), "org": data.get("org"), "city": data.get("city"), "region": data.get("region"), "country": data.get("country_name"), "lat": data.get("latitude"), "lon": data.get("longitude"), "postal": data.get("postal"), "timezone": data.get("timezone"), "company_name": company.get("name"), "company_domain": company.get("domain"), "company_industry": company.get("industry"), "company_size": company.get("size"), "company_logo": company.get("logo_url"), "company_website": company.get("website"), "company_twitter": company.get("twitter"), "company_linkedin": company.get("linkedin"), "company_facebook": company.get("facebook"), "company_instagram": company.get("instagram"), "company_youtube": company.get("youtube"), "company_github": company.get("github"), "company_blog": company.get("blog"), } return result if __name__ == "__main__": test_ip = "8.8.8.8" # Google Public DNS info = get_company_info(test_ip, api_key="YOUR_DEMO_KEY") # replace with real key print(info) ``` **Sample output (using the demo key):** ```json { "ip": "8.8.8.8", "org": "AS15169 Google LLC", "city": "Mountain View", "region": "California", "country": "United States", "lat": 37.386, "lon": -122.0838, "postal": "94035", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles", "company_name": "Google LLC", "company_domain": "google.com", "company_industry": "Internet", "company_size": "10000+ employees", "company_logo": "https://logo.clearbit.com/google.com", "company_website": "https://www.google.com/", "company_twitter": "@google", "company_linkedin": "https://www.linkedin.com/company/google/", "company_facebook": "https://www.facebook.com/Google/", "company_instagram": "https://www.instagram.com/google/", "company_youtube": "https://www.youtube.com/user/Google", "company_github": "https://github.com/google", "company_blog": "https://blog.google/" } ``` --- ## How to choose the right API | Criteria | ipdata.co | ipgeolocation.io | ipstack.com | ipapi.co | ipinfo.io | |----------|-----------|------------------|-------------|----------|-----------| | **Depth of company data** | ★★★★★ | ★★★★☆ | ★★★★☆ | ★★☆☆☆ | ★★☆☆☆ | | **Free quota** | 1 000/day | 1 000/day | 10 000/month | 30 000/month | 50 000/month | | **Demo key** | Yes (demo) | Yes (demo) | Yes (demo) | Yes (demo) | Yes (demo) | | **Rate‑limit flexibility** | 1 000/day (no burst) | 1 000/day (burst allowed) | 10 000/month (burst allowed) | 30 000/month (burst allowed) | 50 000/month (burst allowed) | | **Contact‑style fields** | Full (social, blog, etc.) | Full (social, blog, etc.) | Full (social, blog, etc.) | Limited (`org` only) | Limited (`org` only) | | **Ease of integration** | Very easy (JSON, simple auth) | Very easy | Easy | Easy | Easy | If you need **rich company metadata** (logo, social links, size, industry) and you’re okay with a modest free quota, **ipdata.co** or **ipgeolocation.io** are the best picks. If you need a larger free quota and don’t mind slightly less company detail, **ipstack.com**, **ipapi.co**, or **ipinfo.io** are solid choices. --- ## Next steps 1. Sign up for a free account at the provider of your choice (e.g., [ipdata.co](https://ipdata.co/), [ipgeolocation.io](https://ipgeolocation.io/)). 2. Grab your API key (or use the demo key for quick testing). 3. Plug the key into the example code above (replace `"demo"` or `"YOUR_DEMO_KEY"` with your real key). 4. Run the script and inspect the JSON output. 5. If you need additional fields (e.g., phone numbers, direct emails), check the provider’s documentation – some offer paid tiers that expose those details. Happy hacking!
